headline: Approved ambulance and dispatch agreement with Litchfield starting January 1, 2027; voted 3-2 to rescind legal spending memo.
summary: Residents spoke about legal bills tied to investigations and about the Litchfield deal. The council also approved changes to the Fire Department rules and the General Assistance Guidelines. It also approved fund transfers for West Road pumphouse repairs and new defibrillators.
decisions: Approved 3-2 a motion to rescind the Town Manager's memo on legal spending. The Town Manager said he will not rescind it.
Approved 5-0 reappointing Brian Battaglia to the Southern New Hampshire Planning Commission for a four-year term.
Approved Ordinance 2026-13, amending the Fire Department Rules and Regulations, 5-0.
Adopted the revised General Assistance Guidelines, 5-0.
Scheduled a September 14, 2026 public hearing on PurposeEnergy's application for a Commercial/Industrial Tax Exemption.
Approved up to $22,125.97 from the Recreation Department Capital Reserve Fund for West Road pumphouse repairs, 5-0.
Approved up to $112,475.93 from the Fire Equipment Capital Reserve Fund for the first payment on new defibrillators, 3-0.
Tabled discussion of the easement for the cul-de-sac at the end of Ashley Drive.
Approved authorizing the Town Manager to enter into an agreement with Litchfield for ambulance transport, EMS, and fire dispatch starting January 1, 2027, 5-0.
Continued the Town Manager job description to the next Council meeting.
Agreed to pursue the Braver Angels program to enhance civic discourse.
Approved the consent items, including minutes from August 3, 2026, 5-0.

decision_evidence.quote: Vice Chair Faber moved that the memo be rescinded. Seconded by Councilor Combes. ... Motion carried 3-2-0, with Councilors Paul and Bouchard voting in opposition.

Vice Chair Faber moved that the Londonderry Town Council hereby reappoints Brian Battaglia to the Southern Hampshire Planning Commission for a four-year term beginning on September 1, 2026 and ending on June 30, 2030. Seconded by Chair Combes. Motion carried 5-0-0.

Councilor Bouchard moved that the Londonderry Town Council hereby approves Ordinance 2026-13 amending the Londonderry Fire Department Rules and Regulations as indicated. Seconded by Vice Chair Faber. Motion carried 5-0-0.

Vice Chair Faber moved that that the Londonderry Town Council hereby adopts the revised Town of Londonderry General Assistance Guidelines, as presented. Seconded by Councilor Bouchard. Motion carried 5-0-0.

Discuss and schedule a public hearing for September 14, 2026 regarding an application from PurposeEnergy requesting the Commercial/Industrial Tax Exemption. ... The public hearing will be held on September 14, 2026.

Councilor Bouchard moved that the Londonderry Town Council hereby authorizes the withdrawal request and directs the Town Treasurer to disburse up to $22,125.97 from the Recreation Department Capital Reserve Fund to pay for repairs related to the West Road fields pumphouse system. Seconded by Councilor Paul. Motion carried 5-0-0.

Councilor Bouchard moved that the Londonderry Town Council hereby authorizes the withdrawal request and directs the Town Treasure to disburse up to $112,475.93 from the Fire Equipment Capital Reserve Fund for the first payment to Zoll Medical Corporation for the replacement of the Zoll cardiac monitor/defibrillators. Seconded by Vice Chair Faber. Motion carried 3-0-0.
Discuss and approve the easement for the cul-de-sac at the end of Ashley Drive. ... The Council agreed to table this discussion.

Councilor Bouchard moved that the Londonderry Town Council hereby authorizes the Town Manager to enter into Intermunicipal Agreements with the Town of Litchfield for the Londonderry Fire Department to provide transporting ambulance services in addition to EMS and Fire Dispatch Services beginning on January 1, 2027, for a three-year period. ... Seconded by Vice Chair Faber. Motion carried 5-0-0.
Discuss and approve the Town Manager’s job description for the position of Town Manager. ... The Council agreed to move this topic to the next Council meeting.
Discuss the Town Manager’s recommendation to engage the Braver Angels program to enhance civic discourse. ... The Council agreed to pursue this.

C. TOWN COUNCIL ISSUES 84 
Chair Dunn said the bill for legal services for the Town of Londonderry printed in the 85 
Londonderry Times on August 12th was privileged information and exempt from disclosure 86 
under 91-A. Providing the bill to the press was a violation of the duty of loyalty to the Town 87 
and 91-A, and could place other privileged documents in jeopardy of disclosure. When the 88 
investigation is complete, the results will be presented to the full Council.  89 
 90 
Councilor Paul asked to schedule a virtual meeting between Shaheen & Gordon and all 91 
Councilors to obtain all information that Chair Dunn and Vice Chair Faber have been given. 92

She asked for clarity on the scope of the investigations, whether Councilors are being 93 
investigated, when the investigation process started and when it is expected to end, the 94 
approximate cost of the investigations, and a timeline for the investigations. She asked if a cap 95 
had been set on the cost of the investigations. She said a bill was received for over $21,000 for 96 
approximately 49 hours of work. The full Council should know about and vote on all 97 
interactions with attorneys, and know the details of the investigations.  98 
 99 
Town Manager Mulholland said he did not release privileged information. The legal bill was 100 
provided as part of a response to a 91-A request. The Council is spending public funds and this 101 
cannot be hidden.  102 
 103 
Chair Dunn said a legal protocol for authorization of legal services rendered to the Town was 104 
issued by legal counsel on July 21, 2026, and is a privileged document. The Town Charter 105 
authorizes the Council to initiate investigations and appoint subcommittees. He reviewed 106 
recent legal bills and the associated costs. 107 
 108 
Chair Dunn said the Town Manager sent a memo was sent on July 30, 2026, to the DPW 109 
Director requiring expenditure controls to help address excessive legal expenses incurred in 110 
FY2027. He said legal expenses in FY2026 were largely incurred at the direction of the Town 111 
Manager and not the Council. A legal protocol has been issued stating that the Town Manager 112 
does not have the authority to direct legal counsel. The Council will exercise that authority in 113 
FY2027 with an eye on controlling costs and streamlining legal work on behalf of the Town.  114 
 115 
Chair Dunn said the Council created a special subcommittee to interact with legal counsel to 116 
create a more efficient process, and it will report to the full Council when the investigation is 117 
complete. He said the Town Manager relies in part on RSA 37:6 for his authority to issue the 118 
directive; the RSA states the Town Manager is subject to the direction of the Council. He asked 119 
the Council to discuss the memorandum and ask the Town Manager to withdraw the directive.  120 
 121 
Councilor Bouchard said it is the Town Manager's responsibility to manage the budget and 122 
spoke in support of his actions. He asked how much will be spent on the investigations and 123 
how long they will take, and noted the subcommittee is expending taxpayer funds. A legal bill 124 
for the investigations has not been received. He stressed the need to release the results of the 125 
investigations. He shared an email explaining that privilege is held by the client and can be 126 
waived by the client. 127 
 128 
Councilor Paul asked about a trial date being set regarding the Veterans Tax Credit. She spoke 129 
to the need for transparency on the part of the Chair. She asked that a cap be set on the cost of 130 
the investigations. She asked why the complaint against Councilor Combes was not being 131 
investigated, and from which fiscal year the legal expenses will be paid. 132 
 133 
Councilor Combes noted that all five Councilors would have to waive privilege, not a single 134 
Councilor. He said the legal bills are in line with last year's bills and the Council incurred 9% 135 
of the legal costs. Councilors Paul and Bouchard asked to see this research.  136 
 137 
Vice Chair Faber said it was premature to make recissions, considering the fiscal year began 138
Londonderry Town Council Minutes 8/17/2026 
 
4 
 
on July 1st. The recissions were not appropriate and were excessive, and the Council can 139 
control the legal budget.  140 
 141 
Vice Chair Faber moved that the memo be rescinded. Seconded by Councilor Combes.  142 
 143 
Discussion: Town Manager Mulholland said it is better to make recissions now; if they are 144 
made later, it could result in layoffs. One bill has equaled 10% of the legal budget for the year. 145 
He listed bills that have not been received dating back to April. He said the Council will not 146 
give him projected costs for those services. The Charter assigns him the responsibility of fiscal 147 
management.  148 
 149 
Councilor Combes asked why budget cuts are being suggested, when there was a surplus at the 150 
end of the last fiscal year. Town Manager Mulholland said legal costs were over budget last 151 
year at a cost of $290/hour. The Town is paying $500/hour, $450/hour, and $375/hour this 152 
year, which was not budgeted. Attorneys are being paid to respond to 91-A requests that the 153 
Town normally handles. It is prudent to take action now to reduce the risk of layoffs and cutting 154 
services later.  155 
 156 
Motion carried 3-2-0, with Councilors Paul and Bouchard voting in opposition. Chair votes 157 
in the affirmative. 158 
 159 
Town Manager Mulholland said he will not rescind the memo.  160

 277

 279

2. Discuss and authorize the Intermunicipal Agreement with the Town of Litchfield 289 
for the Londonderry Fire Department to provide Emergency Medical Services and 290 
Fire Dispatch Services. 291 
Chief Young and Deputy Chief LeBlanc reviewed the presentation that was given on 292 
August 3rd regarding providing ambulance and dispatch services to the Town of 293 
Litchfield. Chief Young reviewed the timeline, advantages of the partnership, the 294 
addition of staff and how this will be funded, the cost to provide services, and the 295 
projected revenue. He explained how this proposal would benefit the community, 296 
including providing much-needed staffing. He stressed his personal experience with 297 
providing similar services.  298 
 299 
The Council asked clarifying questions about staffing, insurance reimbursement, 300 
workload, projected cost of providing the service, possible overtime and the impact on 301 
the budget line, and the ability to maintain the level of service to Londonderry. They 302 
expressed concern that the revenue generated is not adequate to cover the cost of offering 303 
this service, and asked the Chief to return with a new proposal that better benefits 304 
Londonderry financially. Chief Young noted that the proposal was very conservative.  305 
 306 
Litchfield Fire Chief Doug Nicoll responded to questions about the population of 307 
Litchfield, and refuted the claim that Hudson is currently subsidizing the service for 308 
Litchfield.  309 
 310 
Deputy Chief LeBlanc spoke as a resident, stating that he would not support something 311 
that was not of benefit to the community.   312 
 313 
Chief Young said this proposal is designed to prevent the taxpayers of Londonderry from 314 
subsidizing this service. He asked for guidance as to what the Council wants in terms of 315

demonstrates that the service will be a net positive for the community. The Council 317 
discussed what they would like to see in a revised proposal.  318

the budget. They asked if the Council supported investing in the partnership and if the 323
